title: Streamlined batch orchestration and cache lifecycle disentanglement
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over time the continuous batching controller, request scheduler, and KV cache lifecycle code paths have accumulated ad-hoc guards, cross-cutting locks, and divergent eviction semantics. This has made it hard to reason about tail latency, caused intermittent cache misses during resizes, and increased risk when changing kernel selection or sequence-length heuristics.

Goal: Refactor the batch orchestration layer to separate scheduling concerns from cache lifecycle management and introduce a clear handoff contract (immutable batch descriptor + transient cache tokens). This reduces lock contention, enables safer unit tests for scheduler logic, and allows us to introduce a low-risk rolling migration to the new cache coordinator.

Scope:
- Rework scheduler state machine to use immutable BatchDescriptor objects and a lightweight lease token for in-flight KV bindings.
- Extract cache lifecycle operations (warmup, index compaction, eviction) into a CacheCoordinator module with explicit async boundaries.
- Remove global scheduler lock and replace with per-batch affinity and a lock-free hot-path for token reads.
- Add compatibility shim so older request formats are accepted during migration.

Non-goals: Full redesign of quantization paths, changing kernel selection heuristics, or altering user-facing batching APIs.

Acceptance criteria:
1) No API changes to callers (backwards compatible).
2) End-to-end p99 generation latency for synthetic T=256 workload improves or remains within 5% of baseline with identical throughput.
3) KV cache hit-rate regression <= 1% on representative workloads.
4) Unit and integration tests covering lease token races and cache compaction scenarios are added to CI.
5) Migration can be toggled via runtime feature flag per-region.

Migration plan: Implement CacheCoordinator behind feature flag; stage rollout on canary fleet (5% capacity) -> monitor latency, error rates, cache hit-rate -> expand to 25% -> full rollout. If cache hit-rate drops or tail latency increases above threshold, rollback to shim.

Testing & Benchmarks: Use perf harness (bench/continuous-batching) with mixed sequence length distribution (short/medium/long) and the existing internal replay traces stored in S3. Benchmark results will be recorded in the runtime-1.26 dashboard.

Risks and mitigations:
- Race conditions during handoff: mitigated by lease token design + property-based tests.
- Minor temporary increase in memory while warmup runs: monitor pod memory and set conservative warmup concurrency.
- Hidden dependency on legacy eviction order: will include a compatibility mode that preserves order for flagged tenants.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Created ticket after postmortem identified cache thrashing during autoscale spike. Meeting with infra and runtime teams scheduled for 2026-02-27.
2026-02-27 - Design sync: agreed on immutable BatchDescriptor and lease-token approach. Decided to extract cache operations into a single CacheCoordinator component to simplify testing.

2026-03-02 - Spike complete: prototype replaced global scheduler lock with per-batch affinity; local benchmarks show 12% reduction in scheduler lock contention on heavy-concurrency trace. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4012 (WIP).

2026-03-05 - Code review feedback: Marco asked to add explicit time-bounded leases to avoid stuck tokens; Aisha to add property-based tests for race scenarios. Added test matrix on macOS and linux runners.

2026-03-08 - Integration test failure observed: cache warmup sequence occasionally delayed when compaction runs concurrently. Investigation points to compaction GC holding a shard-level lock longer than expected. Plan: make compaction cooperative and yield on large shards.
2026-03-10 - Bench run (canary trace set): p50 stable, p95 +2%, p99 +4% — within acceptance envelope. Cache hit-rate change: -0.6%. Will proceed to staged canary rollout behind feature flag.

2026-03-11 - Deployed feature-flagged CacheCoordinator to canary cluster (5%). Observability dashboards added (runtime-1.26 -> scheduling/kv_lifecycle). Watching memory and tail-latency charts closely.

Open questions: Should tenant-level cache metrics be exposed to customers? (Product/PM to decide). Also need to coordinate with Dedicated infra team for reserved-capacity nodes that have longer-lived caches.
